    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that last week in the NFL was full of drama.
    • Fernando Mendoza will make the first road start of his career against an aggressive Denver Broncos defense, the Detroit Lions will begin life without Aidan Hutchinson at home against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, and the Vikings will play the 49ers in Mexico City in what could go down as one of the best primetime matchups of the entire season.
    • There are many, many massive spreads in the NFL this week!
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that last week in the NFL was full of drama. The Cleveland Browns came back from down 17-0 to defeat the Houston Texans, while Kirk Cousins was victorious in his first game back with the Minnesota Vikings. The San Francisco 49ers and Dallas Cowboys put up 86 total points in Arlington, and the Cincinnati Bengals blew out Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers on "Sunday Night Football.".

    This week there's more. Fernando Mendoza will make the first road start of his career against an aggressive Denver Broncos defense, the Detroit Lions will begin life without Aidan Hutchinson at home against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, and the Vikings will play the 49ers in Mexico City in what could go down as one of the best primetime matchups of the entire season.

    There are many, many massive spreads in the NFL this week! Which teams should you pick in Week 11, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 18 over at DraftKings Sportsbook.

    Dajani (Texans -12.5): I would typically lean toward a huge underdog like this in a divisional game, but two factors have me leaning the other way. One, Daniel Jones threw for just 108 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions last week against the Miami Dolphins. They were starting a quarterback that had never played in the NFL, yet only lost by two points. Jones has been terrible. He's turned the ball over an NFL-high 15 times and has the worst record in primetime by any quarterback since 1970 at 1-16. Additionally, the Texans allowed the Browns to come back from down 17-0 and win their meeting last week, which I imagine has this Texans team seeing red. C.J. Stroud and Co. are better than their 3-6 record indicates. They even beat the Jacksonville Jaguars earlier this season. I think the large number is justified. …  Prediction: Texans 27, Colts 14.

    In a recent development, dubin (Colts +12.5): I just don't think the Texans should be favored by 12.5 points over anybody. … Prediction: Texans 23, Colts 13.

    Dajani (Buccaneers +7): Jahmyr Gibbs leads the NFL in rushing yards this season with 1,000, while the Buccaneers allow the fewest rushing yards per game (79.2). The Bucs also lead the NFL in rushing offense and in takeaways with 21. With the Buccaneers coming off their bye week and the Lions coming off an international trip that cost them Aidan Hutchinson for the season, I'm leaning toward Tampa Bay with the points. The Bucs are 4-1 against the spread in their last five games, but keep an eye on the quarterback situation over the next 24 hours. …  Prediction: Lions 24, Buccaneers 21.

    Dubin (Lions -7): The Bucs likely playing this game without Baker Mayfield pushed me in this direction. Jalon Daniels is fine, but I don't expect the passing game to be able to do much here. The Bucs base the entire offense around the run anyway, but the Lions are actually pretty tough to run on. That could change without Aidan Hutchinson, obviously, but I don't think it will change enough for Tampa's offense to keep pace with what the Lions are likely to do. … Prediction: Lions 24, Buccaneers 16.

    It has been revealed that dajani (Broncos -10): I don't think Fernando Mendoza wins his second career start in an environment like Mile High, but can he cover the double-digit spread? Denver has won just one game by double digits this season, back in Week 7 against the Arizona Cardinals. The Las Vegas Raiders, on the other hand, have covered in four straight divisional games for the first time since 2022. The Broncos are coming off their bye week and have scored at least 26 points in each of their last three games. Bo Nix has also thrown multiple touchdowns in back-to-back games. The Raiders are tied for the worst scoring defense in the NFL this year with 28.9 points allowed per game, so I think the Broncos could reach 30 points this week. That could make it tough for Mendoza to cover the spread. He's actually the first rookie quarterback to ever face both of the previous season's No. 1 seeds in his first two career starts. …  Prediction: Broncos 30, Raiders 17.

    Dubin (Raiders +10): The Broncos have seven wins this year, and six of them are by one score. The only team they beat by more than seven points is the Cardinals. I reserve the right to change this pick if Brock Bowers is out and Fernando Mendoza just doesn't have anyone at all to throw the ball to, but otherwise the Broncos just don't seem like a team capable of blowing out an opponent that has actually played fairly well this year. … Prediction: Broncos 21, Raiders 17.

    It has been revealed that dajani (Giants +6): No one is debating that the Jaguars are not one of the best teams in the NFL, but they haven't exactly been tested recently. They blew out the hapless Colts, had no problem with Joe Fagnano's Baltimore Ravens and then dropped 40 points on the one-win Tennessee Titans. The Giants aren't Super Bowl contenders, but this is easily the best team Jacksonville has played in over the past month. I'm not going to take the Giants to win this game straight up, but I am leaning toward the six points. The Giants have an underrated defense that currently ranks No. 5 in the NFL in yards allowed per game (305.7), and J.J. McCarthy has the fifth-most yards per attempt (8.8) since his Giants debut in Week 5. Both of these teams are 6-3 ATS this season. Give me the Giants with a back-door cover. …  Prediction: Jaguars 23, Giants 18.

    Dubin (Jaguars -6): Unlike the Broncos, the Jaguars have blown out everybody. Five of their seven wins have come by 17 points or more, including each of their last three games. The Giants are probably better than the Colts, Ravens and Titans, but I don't see them hanging with this Jacksonville offense — not with the Jags getting their upcoming defensive stalwarts on the field for the first time since the trade deadline. (Jessie Bates III and Jordan Davis sat out last week because they had yet to have their bye and the Jags had already taken theirs.) … Prediction: Jaguars 31, Giants 20.

    Recent findings suggest that dajani (49ers -3): The 49ers are coming off a ridiculous 46-40 win over the Cowboys, where they recorded the most total yards in a road game in franchise history (584) and averaged a whopping 9.4 yards per play. Brock Purdy's offense had three touchdowns of 65+ yards! Christian McCaffrey actually became the first running back in NFL history to record two 65-yard receiving touchdowns in a game. Obviously, the Vikings' defense is MUCH better than the Cowboys', but something you should know is that this game is in Mexico City. And both teams have prepared for it differently.

    According to recent reports, the stadium the 49ers and Vikings will play in on Sunday is over 7,000 feet above sea level. So, the 49ers traveled to the U.S. Air Force Academy in Colorado Springs this week, which is at an elevation of 6,621 feet, to prepare. The Vikings, on the other hand, apparently built an altitude chamber so players can get familiar with "thinner air" before Sunday, but otherwise are seemingly pulling a Los Angeles Rams and just showing up on site the day before the game. The 49ers dominated the Rams in Australia in Week 1, 27-7, and part of that was because their travel looks were so much better. The 49ers have won and covered in four straight International games. …  Prediction: 49ers 26, Vikings 20.

    In a recent development, dubin (49ers -3): In a battle of a great offense against a great defense, I am usually going to lean toward the offensive side unless there's a really compelling reason in favor of the defensive-minded team. Kirk Cousins' ability to elevate the Vikings' own offense almost provides that reason, but it's not quite enough for me to get there. This San Francisco offense is too much of a well-oiled machine for me to pick against the Niners — even in a matchup with a defensive coordinator as crazy and as good as Brian Flores. … Prediction: 49ers 23, Vikings 17.

    Sources indicate that dajani (Bengals -6.5): Before you think this is some easy pick to make just because of how hot the Bengals are, know that Cincy is 0-2-1 in its past three games against the Washington Commanders, who just upset the Giants in New York last week. Jayden Daniels' coming-out party as a rookie actually came against the Bengals. Still, it's hard to go against my Super Bowl pick and my MVP pick this season.

    The Bengals are 6-2 SU and 6-1-1 ATS in their last eight road games and have scored at least 30 points in three straight on the road. Joe Burrow is on pace for the highest completion percentage (74.7%) in a season in NFL history, and he also leads the league in passing yards per game (310.6), passing touchdowns (27) and passer rating (117.7). His MVP case is aided by the dynamic duo of Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, who are on pace to become the first teammate duo to both record 1,500 yards receiving in a season. …  Prediction: Bengals 27, Commanders 20.

    Sources indicate that dubin (Bengals -6.5): The current version of the Commanders does not have the firepower to keep up with the Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins show. I'm not sure any version of the Commanders ever did, but even after winning two of their last three games, they haven't exactly looked impressive. The Bengals, meanwhile, are putting on an aerial assault for the ages every week. … Prediction: Bengals 31, Commanders 20.

    Tari Eason gives amazing, blunt explanation for his 25-point game: 'S--t, the Wizards, for real'

    📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (365 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Houston Rockets improved to 11-3 on the season with a 147-119 beatdown of the Washington Wizards on Sunday night.
    • While Houston is no stranger to an offensive explosion, ranking second in the NBA this season in offensive rating (121.2), the 147 points scored on Sunday were 12 more than they've scored in a game this season.
    • According to recent reports, that 25-point performance represents a new season high for Eason -- his previous best was a 19-point effort against the Hawks -- as he went 10 for 14 from the field and 3 of 5 from 3-point range in 30 minutes off the bench.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Houston Rockets improved to 11-3 on the season with a 147-119 beatdown of the Washington Wizards on Sunday night.

    While Houston is no stranger to an offensive explosion, ranking second in the NBA this season in offensive rating (121.2), the 147 points scored on Sunday were 12 more than they've scored in a game this season. It was a balanced scoring effort as a team, as six players reached double figures and three scored at least 25 points -- including Tari Eason off the bench.

    According to recent reports, that 25-point performance represents a new season high for Eason -- his previous best was a 19-point effort against the Hawks -- as he went 10 for 14 from the field and 3 of 5 from 3-point range in 30 minutes off the bench. That effort earned Eason the honor of the walk-off TV interview, during which he gave a brutally honest (and hilarious) answer for why he was able to set a new season high and do so efficiently.

    "Shit, the Wizards, for real. It was them," Eason said.

    Tari Eason on what allowed him to have a season-high 25 points off the bench tonight:"Shit, the Wizards, for real." pic.twitter.com/t4bOwtzw5r.

    A+ work here, no notes. Eason could've puffed out his chest after beating up on the Wizards or complimented his teammates for allowing him to get in a rhythm, but instead chose the honest route rarely taken by players in a post-game interview and simply admitted that anyone could get buckets on Washington.

    According to recent reports, the Wizards are not the worst defense in the NBA -- that honor belongs to the Chicago Bulls -- but they are 25th in defensive rating and certainly do not boast very many elite defenders. Clearly, Eason didn't feel like he was doing anything special or out of the ordinary on Sunday night on his way to 25 points off the bench, and gave credit where it was due to the other team.

    Unfortunately for the Wizards, it is not credit they'd like to take, and this feels like the kind of (earned) disrespect that should light some kind of fire under Washington.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Everton appear well ahead of Newcastle United in their preparation for the new Premier League season after a comfortable 3-1 victory at Murrayfield.

    On a sobering evening for newly introduced Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle, who changed all 10 outfield players at half-time, Everton’s one and two-touch attacking play proved difficult to contain.

    Everton took the lead through Thierno Barry after a defensive error from Sven Botman, before Iliman Ndiaye scored a penalty that was won cheaply by summer signing Hayden Hackney.

    Newcastle’s raft of half-time changes helped David Moyes’s team strengthen their grip further, with Tyrique George adding a stylish third and 19-year-old Harrison Armstrong providing his second assist of the game.

    Among the Newcastle players introduced at half-time was 18-year-old Sean Steur, the exciting midfield prospect signed from Ajax this summer. Aladji Bamba and Bazoumana Toure also flickered with promise, but a sharp start from Jaissle’s team faded.

    They pulled a goal back late on when Jacob Murphy’s cross found Harvey Barnes at the back post, but they offered little as an attacking force throughout the second half.

    Newcastle have two more friendlies, against Bayer Leverkusen and Strasbourg, before they begin their Premier League season at home to Liverpool.

    The club are reeling from the summer departures of Bruno Guimaraes, Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and manager Eddie Howe, but David Hopkinson, the chief executive, struck a bullish tone when he spoke of this being the start of “Newcastle 2.0”.

    Everton look the more settled side and club, and the performances of new arrivals Hackney and George were encouraging, while Thierno Barry was sharp in the centre-forward position that has proved so difficult for the club to fill in recent seasons.

    Everton kick-off their newly introduced season at home to Crystal Palace, and keeping Ndiaye at the club beyond the end of the transfer window will be a priority.

    According to recent reports, the scoreline is a fair reflection of the game. Everton looked sharper, as well as fitter, and there are more positives for them to take. They look ready for the newly introduced season, Newcastle need reinforcements.

    Recent findings suggest that alcaraz bends a shot not far wide from 25 yards for Everton. The game is meandering towards its conclusion now.

    Willock collects the ball between the lines, feeds Murphy wide right, and his ball across goal is turned in at the back post by Harvey Barnes.

    Moyes makes another pair of changes: Keane and Hackney off, O’Brien and Foster on.

    Everton fans are enjoying themselves now, belting out Spirit of the Blues at Murrayfield.

    More defending for Newcastle to do but they deal with Hackney’s corner delivery. All too easy for Everton to slice through their midfield in the build up though.

    That goal had been coming, and Tyrique George is heavily involved again. He carries the ball forward and finds Armstrong, who returns the favour. George shoots on the swivel and picks out the bottom corner.

    If I were a Newcastle fan in the stands, Edinbugh’s city centre hostelries would be looking very alluring just about now. There is not much for them to watch in this season half, they are chasing shadows. Some of that can be put down to the handful of young plyers in their second-half XI.

    Tyler Dribbling drops a shoulder down the right, and wins a corner off Harvey Barnes. Everton are finishing this game the stronger, there are more goals in this should they put their foot on the pedal.

    Industry observers note that newcastle, with some youngsters in their defence, looking a little ragged against Everton’s direct attacks now, but George runs into traffic at the edge of the box. Then Alcaraz is booked for a cynical foul.

    Three more Everton changes on the way: Beto, Dibling and Alcaraz on for Barry, Ndiaye and Dewsbury-Hall.

    Hayden Hackney plays a one-two with Tyrique George for Everton, with the former Chelsea winger backheeling the ball into Hackney’s path, and there were unheeded calls for a penalty. It was more of a penalty than the one Everton were awarded in the first half, Lewis Miley tripped him.

    It has been revealed that the upstart Chicago White Sox have added one of the game's hardest-throwing pitchers to their rotation. Chicago and righty Dustin May have agreed to a three-year contract worth $52.5 million, reports FanSided.

    May, 29, split this past season between the St. Louis Cardinals and World Series champion Milwaukee Brewers. He threw a career-high 145 ⅔ innings with a 4.70 ERA, though the underlying numbers (3.63 FIP and 4.50 expected ERA) were more respectable. May's 96.9 mph average fastball velocity was 15th highest among the 141 pitchers with at least 100 innings in 2026.

    Recent findings suggest that rotation help was a priority for a White Sox team that reached the postseason for the first time since 2021, but used openers and bullpen games regularly throughout the season. Only twice in seven postseason games did Chicago use a traditional starting pitcher. Here is the team's updated rotation depth chart:.

    Castillo struggled badly (30 runs in 31 innings) after coming over from the Seattle Mariners at the trade deadline, and finished the season on the injured list with a shoulder issue. His $22.75 million salary could land him in the rotation on Opening Day, though the White Sox have enough options to replace him should Castillo remain ineffective.

    In a recent development, we ranked May as the offseason's 25th-best free agent, and the 11th-best starting pitcher. Here's a snippet of the write-up:.

    May turned only 29 in September and he's topped 130 innings in back-to-back years after throwing 101 innings total around injuries, including UCL surgery, from 2021-24. Even after the injuries, May still lives in the mid-to-upper-90s with his sinker, and pitch data models are fond of his sweeper and curveball. It is not the best sign, though, that the Brewers, who know pitching as well as any team, couldn't fully unlock May after making him their significant deadline rotation addition. Still, the combination of age and high-octane stuff makes him a nice upside play ...

    May made two starts and three relief appearances during Milwaukee's postseason run. If the White Sox opt to use bullpen games again next year, he is familiar and capable in that role.     There is no wider gap between two divisions in NFL history than the 2026 NFC North and the 2026 NFC South.

    The NFC North is a combined 27-10 this season, which is on pace to be the best mark by a division since the 1970 merger. If the playoffs started today, the NFC North would be the first division to have four playoff teams since 1998, when there were only three divisions per conference. Yes, the group is that good.

    The NFC South, meanwhile, is a combined 13-24. That is on pace to be the second-worst mark since the merger. (Take a bow, 2008 NFC West). Currently, the Panthers lead this woebegone division at 4-5. According to CBS Sports forecasting and projections, not a single team from the division is on pace to hit even eight wins. Compare that to the NFC North, where all four teams are projected to hit at least nine; the Packers are barely short of making it so all teams are projected to hit 10 wins.

    Yes, the NFC South is that bad.

    Whether collectively good or collectively bad, they share one thing in common: extremely competitive. And that's what matters when looking at the Week 11 games that will most impact the playoff races.

    The Lions, meanwhile, need to keep collecting wins when they're favored, especially given that they're not only fighting for the NFC North crown but a wild card spot if they fall short in the division.     #3251. Tech Report: How have the Heat turned their season around? Giannis and Bam are on fire, but that's not all

    📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1408 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: How have the Heat turned their season around? Giannis and Bam are on fire, but that's not all

    📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1408 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Since opening up 0-4, the Miami Heat have slowly, quietly, been finding their way into the light.
    • Let's take a look at four major reasons.
    • Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo have combined for 128 points, 42 rebounds and 17 assists on 72% shooting over these last two wins.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Since opening up 0-4, the Miami Heat have slowly, quietly, been finding their way into the light. It initially came against weaker opponents, with wins over the Pacers, Clippers, Jazz and Kings getting them back near .500. But these back-to-back wins over Cleveland (on Friday) and Detroit (on Saturday) put a real stamp on this stretch. After all the panic, Miami has won seven of nine and is tied for the East's No. 4 seed entering this week.

    How have they turned things around? Let's take a look at four major reasons.

    Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo have combined for 128 points, 42 rebounds and 17 assists on 72% shooting over these last two wins. The concerns over their offensive fit -- as relative non-shooters who operate largely in the same spots -- have quieted, but also a good bit of this production is coming independent of one another as Erik Spoelstra is staggering their minutes between the start of each half and fourth-quarter closing time.

    With shooters all around, Adebayo and Antetokounmpo are free to attack maximum interior space and exploit soft midrange spots, which has been the bread and butter of this run.

    Every mid range jumper from Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo against Cleveland last night: pic.twitter.com/jeamVaSLhk.

    Recent findings suggest that as pointed out by Couper Moorhead of NBA.com, the Heat face more drop-coverage defense (when the massive who's guarding the ball screener falls back toward the rim rather than stepping up to the level of the screen or even higher to contest the shooter coming off the screen) than any other offense in the league. That's because nobody fears Miami's pull-up 3-point shooters, and because Giannis and Bam are such forceful attackers of the rim.

    The soft spot is in between, outside the restricted circle but inside the 3-point line, or even better inside the free-throw line. It's the dreaded midrange zone, where defenses are happy to, concede shots to players like Giannis and Bam, and right now they are both knocking these supposedly inefficient looks down at ridiculous rates.

    Recent findings suggest that these are by far career-high percentages for both guys, and they are coming on career-high frequencies from these zones (over 30% of their total shot attempts in the 3-10 range). Over these last nine games, Giannis is a scorching 22 for 33 from 10-19 feet while Adebayo -- who has also been the best post scorer in the league at 1.26 PPP on 4.8 post-ups per game -- is 30 for 44 from 5-14 feet.

    It has been revealed that they are absolutely wearing these outer-paint shots out, and if defenses keep with the drop coverage, these shots are likely to remain consistently available. It's not to say they'll keep making them at this rate, of course. But to have established these go-zones is a massive step for Miami's half-court offense, because we all know how dangerous they are in the open floor as the highest-frequency and second-highest-scoring transition team.

    Now add in the fact that Miami kills teams on the glass with Giannis and Bam on the court (over these last nine, they are grabbing 78.7 percent of all available defensive rebounds and 37.8% of all offensive rebounds, both of which would lead the league), and in the turnover battle, and what you have is a Heat team that is getting a lot more true shot attempts than its opponents (almost 10 more per 100 possessions).

    That is everything in today's possession-obsessed NBA. Get up more shots than your opponent by generating second-chance opportunities on the offensive boards and by creating more turnovers than you cough up, and you're in a good spot. Make those extra shots at the rate Miami is right now, and you're almost unbeatable.

    Industry observers note that mitchell has gone from a guy perhaps playing to stay in the league, or at least in an NBA rotation, to a current top-three Most Improved Player candidate at FanDuel (+900). He's blowing his previous production away.

    The Heat are a low-volume pick-and-roll team for the same reasons they're a prime candidate for drop coverage: They don't have those kinds of pull-up shooters. Mitchell can punish drops with pull-up 3s on occasion (8 for 20 so far, per Synergy), but more importantly he's the one most often hitting Bam and Giannis in those soft-pocket midrange spots we talked about -- in addition to the rim rolls, cuts and kick-out 3s that open up as he breaches the paint, often in transition.

    Of Mitchell's 119 assists so far, 55 have gone to Giannis and Bam, and he has directly set up a 3-point make 37 times. Those 9.2 assists per game lead the league among qualified players, and the 257 points his assists have generated rank second only to Trae Young's 260, per PBP Stats. Young is making $49 million this year. Mitchell is making $12 million.

    In a recent development, then there is the shooting. Mitchell has steadily improved from range throughout his career, but this season he's on fire at 43% on catch-and-shoot 3s, per Synergy, as part of Miami's spacing around Bam and Giannis. We saw all of Mitchell's tools in his 22-point/17-assist masterpiece against Cleveland.

    Davion Mitchell ABSURD statline vs Cavs: 22 PTS | 5 REB | 17 AST | 7/14 FG | 66 TS% pic.twitter.com/b0d8I1XHDy.

    Industry observers note that thompson isn't the player he was in his prime. His defense has especially declined, and he's not going to be putting up any more 37-point quarters. But he's still a sniper.

    Thompson is splashing 42% on almost 10 3s a game, and his 48 total 3-pointers rank third league-wide, and his 15.3 PPG are the most he's averaged since leaving Golden State. He's been especially hot of late, averaging 20 PPG on 48/45 shooting splits over his last seven games.

    Klay Thompson was amazing vs the Pistons26 PTS - 4 AST - 6 3PM - 10/17 FGM Found a upcoming home pic.twitter.com/JvQju9Hais.

    Industry observers note that over the last seven games, Miami is plus-11.7 with Thompson on the court and minus-3.7 when he's off. That's the best split on the team. The starting lineup of Mitchell, Bam, Giannis, Thompson and Pelle Larsson (who has been significant in this turnaround, too, since his promotion to the first five), the Heat are outscoring opponents by 23 points per 100 possessions, and Thompson has been particularly effective playing alongside Giannis. With those two on the court as Bam rests, Miami is drumming teams by 31.6 points per 100, per Databallr.

    In a recent development, miami's defense was expected to be a strength, and when people looked up and saw a bottom-barrel rating, it was jarring. Some of that, if not most of it, could be attributed to inordinately hot shooting by their opponents, which wasn't likely to continue. And indeed it hasn't.

    It has been revealed that through the first seven games, Miami opponents were shooting 41.8% from 3 and 50% from the midrange, per Cleaning the Glass. That made for a 58.7 effective field-goal percentage, despite Miami's defense registering a top-three expected eFG% (52.9) based on the shots they were surrendering, per Cleaning the Glass.

    According to recent reports, translation: the Heat were, and are, forcing generally inefficient shots, but to start the year those shots were going in at a rate of almost 6% better than expected. That was the worst, or unluckiest, mark in the league, however you want to look at it.

    In a recent development, cut to this four-game win streak, over which opponents are down to 35.2% from 3 with a 53.9 eFG% against an expected 54%, per CTG. That's in part because Miami has cut the number of wide-open 3s (nearest defender at least six feet away) it was allowing to start the year almost in half (to start, they were surrendering 16 wide-open 3s every night, but over this four-game winning streak they are down to 9.1, stingiest in the league). Even better, their opponents have come down from a 45.5% conversion rate on those wide-open 3s to 40%.

    Industry observers note that all of which is to say, Miami's opponent shooting is coming back to earth. Hot shooting can render any defense helpless, but over time, if you're forcing a team into tough shots from tough spots, the averages are going to swing back your way eventually. Miami is starting to see that happen.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The annual GM Meetings came and went last week with two significant transactions.
    • Industry observers note that otherwise, we're still waiting on the winter's first true blockbuster, and the clock is ticking with a lockout expected upon the collective bargaining agreement's expiration at 11:59 p.m.
    • Teams are calling the Rangers about left-hander MacKenzie Gore, who is a year away from free agency, according to The Athletic.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The annual GM Meetings came and went last week with two significant transactions. The Braves signed reliever Evan Phillips (three years and $35 million) and the Red Sox signed slugger Jake Bauers (four years and $58 million). Bauers will give Boston some desperately needed home run power. Phillips will pair with Robert Suarez in the late innings for Atlanta.

    Industry observers note that otherwise, we're still waiting on the winter's first true blockbuster, and the clock is ticking with a lockout expected upon the collective bargaining agreement's expiration at 11:59 p.m. ET on Dec. 1. Here are our top 50 free agents and top 25 trade candidates, and the important offseason dates and deadlines you need to know. Here now are Tuesday's hot stove happenings.

    Teams are calling the Rangers about left-hander MacKenzie Gore, who is a year away from free agency, according to The Athletic. There is some reluctance to trade for players with only one year of control because games could be lost to a work stoppage next year, but pitching is so in-demand that at least some clubs are exploring a deal for Gore.

    Industry observers note that now 27, Gore is one of only six pitchers to make at least 30 starts in each of the last three years. His under-the-hood numbers (3.87 FIP and 4.19 expected ERA) were much better than his 4.58 actual ERA, plus he has long been considered to have untapped upside. Gore will give you innings, at minimum, and there's a chance his best days are ahead of him.

    According to recent reports, the Red Sox are exploring the trade market for righties Kutter Crawford, Tanner Houck, and Johan Oviedo, according to WEEI. They are also believed to be preparing to trade Jarren Duran, reports MassLive.com. Duran is a potential non-tender candidate if the Red Sox are unable to find a trade partner prior to Friday's deadline. The Mariners and Phillies are among the teams that are "poking around.".

    Crawford, Houck, and Ovideo all missed significant time with injuries in 2026 (Crawford has not appeared in an MLB game since 2024) and are far down Boston's rotation depth chart. Duran has been pushed out of the everyday lineup by the recent Jake Bauers signing. Exploring trades for these four players in a seller's market is a sensible approach.

    According to recent reports, the Mets had an in-person meeting with top-ranked free agent Tarik Skubal on Monday, reports the New York Post. Owner Steve Cohen and president of baseball operations David Stearns were among those in attendance, according to SNY. Skubal and agent Scott Boras will meet with the Blue Jays, Dodgers, Padres, and potentially two other teams in the coming days.

    Skubal is expected to sign before the lockout and is therefore working on a tight schedule, much tighter than usual for top Boras clients. Nolan McLean and Christian Scott give the Mets two promising young arms to build around, but they need to improve the rotation around them, and Skubal would give the club a no-doubt ace to lead the pitching staff.

    In a recent development, the pitching-needy Cubs have shown interest in free agent lefty Trevor Rogers, reports The Athletic. Chicago needs multiple starters this offseason and has cast a wide net in their search. Justin Steele (UCL) and Ben Brown (neck), ostensibly the Cubs' No. 1 and 2 starters, are both recovering from surgeries, and Brown is expected to miss the start of 2027.

    In a recent development, we ranked Rogers as the third-best free agent available this offseason because he is very good as is, and because he'll make analytical models hum with the quality of his arsenal and strike-throwing. Nine pitchers made at least nine starts for the Cubs in 2026 and only two -- Javier Assad and Edward Cabrera -- at the moment remain under contract/team control.

    Sources indicate that the AL East rival Orioles and Yankees are among the teams with interest in free agent slugger Randy Arozarena, according to the Baltimore Banner and New York Post. The O's also have some interest in re-signing Luis Robert Jr. Other than Dylan Beavers and maybe Tyler O'Neill, Baltimore's outfield is wide open right now. They have DH at-bats available too.

    It is likely the Yankees checked in on Arozarena out of due diligence more than serious interest. His righty bat would help their lefty-heavy lineup, though he would be a clunky roster fit as a corner outfielder who really needs to DH on a team that already has plenty of corner outfielders who really need to DH. If Arozarena's market is slow to develop, perhaps New York would pounce.

    Industry observers note that teams around the league believe the Rockies are more open to trading All-Star catcher Hunter Goodman now than they were at the trade deadline, reports MLB Network. Colorado is remarked to have set a very high asking price for Goodman, who in 2026 became just the tenth primary catcher with a 40-homer season. He hit more homers on the road (25) than at Coors Field (16) too.

    Industry observers note that ryan Jeffers and Carson Kelly represent viable free agent alternatives to Goodman as right-handed offense-first catchers, though Goodman is several years younger than both and will have a lower salary the next three years through arbitration. Teams will likely feel more confident in Goodman holding his production for another few years than Jeffers and Kelly.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that during the New England Patriots' Super Bowl loss to the Seattle Seahawks last season, the Seattle defense dominated the New England offense up front.
    • And it's possible that the player who actually allowed the fewest pressures among that group — right tackle Morgan Moses was actually the culprit.
    • Industry observers note that former NFL analytics staffer Ryan Paganetti analyzed hundreds of Patriots offensive snaps and found a tell in Moses' stance that tipped opposing defenses off to whether each play would be a pass or a run.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that during the New England Patriots' Super Bowl loss to the Seattle Seahawks last season, the Seattle defense dominated the New England offense up front. It was a huge part of the game. The Seahawks registered six sacks on Drake Maye, and the Patriots' offensive line allowed 25 total pressures on 57 dropbacks — a 43.8% pressure rate, according to Pro Football Focus.

    And it's possible that the player who actually allowed the fewest pressures among that group — right tackle Morgan Moses was actually the culprit.

    Industry observers note that former NFL analytics staffer Ryan Paganetti analyzed hundreds of Patriots offensive snaps and found a tell in Moses' stance that tipped opposing defenses off to whether each play would be a pass or a run. When Moses lined up with his hands clasped together on his knee while the Patriots were in shotgun, Upcoming England passed 90% of the time, Paganetti noted. And when Moses lined up with his hands apart, the Patriots ran the ball 78% of the time.

    Recent findings suggest that paganetti notes Moses had this tell during much of last year and during the Super Bowl, and infers it may have continued for part of this season. He said he was planning on posting about the tell before Week 1, but "a player on another team encouraged [him] to hold it because they wanted to use it themselves against New England.".

    Did this offensive lineman’s stance tell help decide the Super Bowl?I classified every Patriots early down snap for the whole season entering the Super Bowl (situations where they could plausibly run or pass) and found a glaring tendency from right tackle Morgan Moses.… pic.twitter.com/sziGDRWxau.

    The reason this is particularly notable is that Seahawks defensive back Devon Witherspoon claimed after the Super Bowl that the Seahawks did have a tell on the Patriots' offensive linemen coming into the game.

    According to recent reports, "I knew what was going on," Witherspoon told SiriusXM NFL Radio at the time. "We had a good tell on what they like to do and how they like to play and how they were going to attack us.".

    Witherspoon specifically noted the offensive linemen were the ones who had the tell.

    Recent findings suggest that "We had a tell on their guards and their tackles; how they like to set, they're going to overset on certain rushes," Witherspoon said after the Super Bowl. "They're going to fall for certain moves any time a group of guys get after them, and today I think we did that.".

    It's possible that other teams noticed this trend and have used it against Moses, who has not had his best year in 2026.

    Sources indicate that this season, Moses' 13.9% pressure rate allowed is the fourth-highest among all offensive linemen with at least 100 pass-blocking snaps, according to NFL.com's Next Gen Stats. Moses has done okay in terms of quick pressure rate (2.6%) and sack rate (1.1%), where his numbers are in line with the rest of his career, but the high total pressure rate could be due, at least in part, to opposing defensive lines getting a hint as to whether a particular play will be a pass or a run.

    Paganetti is a reliable source for nuggets like this. He spent several years working with NFL teams in analytics and game management, including for the Eagles, Jaguars, and Raiders. He spent the 2025 season with Las Vegas, which faced the Patriots in Week 1 of the 2025 season.

    Paganetti mentioned he noticed this tell from Moses before that game, and the Raiders used it in route to a 20-13 upset over the eventual AFC Champions. Earlier this season, Paganetti also discovered a distracting video board tactic Fresh England used against opposing kickers under Bill Belichick. Because of that discovery, the NFL eventually changed the rules for what teams can put on their video boards during field goals.

    #3242. Industry News: The 49ers' Fountain of Youth: Can the NFL's oldest and most injured team win the Super Bowl?

    Industry News: The 49ers' Fountain of Youth: Can the NFL's oldest and most injured team win the Super Bowl?

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2014 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It's time to call off the search, Ponce de León, the San Francisco 49ers have struck gold once again.
    • Industry observers note that sometimes all we can do is turn to an old legend to explain how a bunch of geriatrics subdued Father Time and a substation (theory) up to this point.
    • As the 49ers prepare for one of the biggest games of the year vs.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It's time to call off the search, Ponce de León, the San Francisco 49ers have struck gold once again. They've found the Fountain of Youth.

    Industry observers note that sometimes all we can do is turn to an old legend to explain how a bunch of geriatrics subdued Father Time and a substation (theory) up to this point. They've raced out to an 8-1 start despite having the oldest (28.4 average age) and most injured (19.7 player games missed due to injury per game) team in the National Football League.

    As the 49ers prepare for one of the biggest games of the year vs. the Vikings in Mexico City on Sunday (between scheme gods Kyle Shanahan and Brian Flores), I'm marveling at just how incredible they've been at the midway point.

    Kyle Shanahan and Brock Purdy are in their bag, and Christian McCaffrey is still one of the league's best weapons at age 30, even after a season with 450 touches.

    George Kittle is cooking at age 33, less than a year removed from a torn Achilles. Trent Williams (age 38) is still trucking upfield, leading convoys. Purdy-to-Mike-Evans (age 33) was the league's best combo until Evans got hurt. Deebo Samuel (age 30) has even turned back the clock.

    Sources indicate that nobody is using the peanut punch like Fred Warner, who just turned 30 on Thursday. Nick Bosa (age 29) is working his way back into form after his calf injury (and last year's torn ACL). It won't be long before trade deadline acquisitions Keenan Allen (34) and DeForest Buckner (32) get in on the act, too.

    It's incredible when you consider the injury history of some of those guys. I'm just going to assume doctors replaced some of those broken bones and torn ligaments with some 'Terminator' stuff because they are straight-up bots.

    The old guard has stunningly remained intact up to this point. The same can't be stated about the rest of the team. The 49ers' entire WR core and defensive line have been wiped out. At one point, the 49ers' top six wideouts entering the year were out: Mike Evans, Ricky Pearsall, De'Zhaun Stribling, Deebo Samuel, Christian Kirk and Demarcus Robinson.

    In a recent development, injuries ravaged the d-line with Nick Bosa, Mykel Williams, Alfred Collins, C.J. West and Gracen Halton out at different times. Kyle Juszczyk, Mike Evans and Dre Greenlaw have notably missed action as well.

    It's not shocking to see the 49ers playing well, especially given how they persevered last year, but they are taking it to a completely different level this season.

    Sources indicate that this is the most decorated offense on paper in NFL history. The 49ers have the most combined Pro Bowl selections (48) on offense by any team in NFL history. It's an embarrassment of riches, but it doesn't always translate. San Francisco is certainly cashing in, though, with one of the most efficient offenses in modern history.

    They have the highest success rate (55.2%) of any offense in a season this century. Meaning, they keep their offense on schedule, ahead of the chains, better than any unit ever recorded. Overall, they have the most efficient unit, in terms of EPA per play (0.19), since the 2018 Chiefs, when Patrick Mahomes threw for 50 touchdown passes. San Francisco is scoring touchdowns at the third-highest rate (39% of drives) since 2000, behind the 2007 Patriots (who went 16-0 with MVP Tom Brady tossing 50 touchdowns) and the 2020 Packers (with MVP Aaron Rodgers, who had 48 touchdowns and five interceptions).

    Brock Purdy has the highest EPA per dropback (0.34) since Lamar Jackson in 2019, his unanimous MVP year.

    Amazingly, they are in the company of legends despite having the oldest offense, weighted by playing time, since at least 2010 (30.0).

    And the most stunning part is how they are doing it. It's crazy to see their old core look like they are still in their primes. Deebo Samuel was clocked at his fastest speed in two years (20.39 MPH) when he took this hook-and-ladder 80 yards to the house. He made another house call at 19.96 MPH in Dallas last week.

    HOOK-AND-LADDER TD 🤯Deebo Samuel traveled a total distance of 110.35 yards and reached a max speed of 20.39 MPH on this 80-yard touchdown, per @NextGenStats @AZvsSF on FOX/FOX OneStream on #NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/88dsZtSZum.

    Christian McCaffrey turned Jerry World into a track meet with a 66-yard TD reception to ice the game, where he was clocked at 20.29 MPH. That was his fastest speed in over three years and faster than any Jahmyr Gibbs play this year.

    Christian McCaffrey reached 20.29 MPH on this play. That's his fourth-fastest speed since joining the 49ers and his top speed in a game since Week 14 of 2023. pic.twitter.com/TJnSOYzRw3.

    According to recent reports, perhaps the most shocking was George Kittle getting clocked at his fastest speed in seven years earlier this season vs. Denver, nine months removed from his Achilles injury.

    George Kittle reached 19.84 mph on this play, per Next Gen Stats. That's the same speed as Xavier Worthy's 41-yard TD today. It doesn't make sense for a player fresh off an Achilles injury to hit these kinda speeds so soon.He's a freak. pic.twitter.com/NPYVdpKeaD.

    See what I'm saying?! They have literally found the Fountain of Youth. They account for five of the longest touchdowns by 30+ year olds this year. Last week, they became the first team ever with three 50-yard scores in a game from 30+ year olds and the first team, regardless of age, with three 65-yard scores since the 2000 "greatest show on turf" Rams.

    Longest TD Scored by Age 30+ players this yearDeebo Samuel 80 yards (49ers)Christian McCaffrey 74 yards (49ers)Deebo Samuel 70 yards (49ers)Christian McCaffrey 66 yards (49ers)George Kittle 56 yards (49ers).

    Sources indicate that they are going to obliterate old man records. The 49ers have 30 touchdowns from 30+ year olds this season, putting them on pace for 56! The record is 36 by the 1994 49ers and 2002 Raiders.

    They are on pace for 5,028 scrimmage yards from 30-somethings. The only team with 4,000 was the 2002 Raiders (5,016), who were anchored by Jerry Rice and Tim Brown.

    The 49ers are responsible for 22% of the league's touchdowns from 30-plus year olds, and no other team has more than 13.

    They have 555 yards worth of touchdowns from 30-plus-year-olds. No other team has cracked 500 this year, from all players! It's just silly.

    If you weighted their age by scrimmage yards only, the only squad in league history older than this 49ers team is the aforementioned early-2000s Raiders.

    It goes beyond age and scoring. I can confidently say we have never seen a team quite like the 49ers, at least in modern times.

    As mentioned off the top, the 49ers are the oldest and most injured team in the league this year.

    I looked at every team since 2010, using data from SportRadar, to dive a little deeper.

    That's 544 team seasons in that span. The 2026 49ers have the sixth-most games missed due to injury (19.7 per game) and the third-oldest (28.4) roster among those 544 teams. That is why, in the illustration below comparing age and injuries, the 49ers are light years away from all other teams in that span.

    They are the only team of the 544 to rank top among the top three in a season in each of the following: Win percentage, oldest team, and most injured team.

    According to recent reports, those numbers are madness. They defy logic, right? Teams aren't supposed to be this good when they are this old and injured. So can they sustain it and win their first Super Bowl since the 1994 season?

    General manager John Lynch addressed the age concerns last week on KNBR's morning show, "Murph & Markus".

    "I don't think that's a conscious thing. We're not saying, 'Let's go find every old guy.' I've talked about it a lot, and we really feel [this]," Lynch said. "We think it's a good mix because we have those vets, and it's skewed a little bit. Our long snapper [Jon Weeks] is 40 years old. I don't worry about that. He snaps the football and that's tough to do, and he does it very well. Weeks, Trent Williams, I'll take that. [Williams] defies age and the things. I do think there's some level of, 35 is the fresh 30.

    "These guys are taking such great care of themselves, but I feel really good that we've insulated ourselves with that core group, but then we've got a lot of young contributors. You saw [linebacker Jaden Dugger] with the pick-six, Romello Height, god bless Gracen Halton because that was tough to see him going out. Upton Stout, Renardo Green are young players. We've got young players all over playing integral roles. I think it's a really good mix.".

    Here's the blueprint they are trying to follow. It's the 1998 Broncos with John Elway, Michael Jordan's "Last Dance" with the 1998 Bulls, and the 2001 Diamondbacks with old horses like Randy Johnson and Curt Schilling. Those are the oldest teams in each respective sport to win titles in modern history.

    The Patriots had the oldest team in the league in 2018 when they won their last title with Tom Brady.

    Sources indicate that it's also been done before, by a Shanahan. The 49ers are the oldest team (28.4) to start 8-1 or better since the 1998 Broncos, coached by Kyle Shanahan's dad, Mike. Those Broncos are the only team older than these 49ers to win a Super Bowl.

    Recent findings suggest that so age is not the problem. Old teams can win, and analysis of those 544 seasons since 2010 indicates there's even a slight correlation between older teams and more winning.

    The key then is the 49ers' health, specifically their aging studs. They've proven they can produce like Hall of Famers in their prime, but can they stay on the field in January and February?

    According to recent reports, this team is traveling 38,105 miles and crossing 58 time zones (both shattering NFL records) over 17 regular season games. Home-field advantage would be massive for them. Either way, 20 to 21 games when you include playoffs is quite the toll, especially when they are playing in one of the toughest divisions in football and still have games left vs. the Vikings, Seahawks, Giants, Rams and Chiefs.

    In a recent development, the 1998 Broncos team had seven Pro Bowlers in their thirties, the most by any team since 1970. None of those seven (John Elway, Ed McCaffrey, Shannon Sharpe, Mark Schlereth, Tony Jones, Bill Romanowski, Steve Atwater) missed a playoff game.

    The stars would need to align for San Francisco, too. Up to this point, their core of Brock Purdy, Christian McCaffrey, George Kittle, Mike Evans, Trent Williams, Nick Bosa, and Fred Warner have combined to miss just eight games this year (three by Evans, five by Bosa).

    How can we trust the 49ers' track record here?

    Sources indicate that last year, their top six highest-paid players missed 64 games. The year prior, they were ravaged by the most significant injuries to star players the league has ever seen.

    Let's drop Evans from the equation because this is his first year with the 49ers.     This season's NBA Rookie of the Year race has the potential to be one of the closest in league history. While there is no 65-game requirement to win the award — unlike MVP, Defensive Player of the Year and All-NBA honors — playing as many games as possible will be paramount this season in order to claim Rookie of the Year.

    Recent findings suggest that that's why Chicago Bulls forward Caleb Wilson faces an uphill climb to win the honor after fracturing his right hand earlier this month. Wilson is set to miss the next 3-5 weeks and will likely lose serious ground to others in his class. He at the moment has the sixth-best odds (+4000) on FanDuel Sportsbook to win Rookie of the Year.

    Sources indicate that during the first month of the season, three players have separated themselves at the top: Yaxel Lendeborg, Cameron Boozer, and Darius Acuff Jr. While it's not a guarantee one of those players wins it, if the season ended today, those would be the top vote-getters.

    Darryn Peterson and AJ Dybantsa — the first two picks of the 2026 NBA Draft — have some ground to make up during the next four months to get back in the mix.

    With the regular season almost a quarter of the way complete, let's dive into our first Rookie of the Year rankings. All odds via FanDuel.

    It has been revealed that with Steph Curry out, Lendeborg has continued to step up. The oldest player drafted in the first round is coming off a lackluster showing against the Spurs in the NBA Cup, but before that he had three straight games of 23+ points. He is shooting 48.6% from the field and 41.4% from 3. Lendeborg didn't start shooting 3s on a consistent basis until he got to Michigan last season, so knocking down that percentage on 5.4 attempts per night is a positive sign. Fourteen games into the season, Lendeborg is the favorite.

    Sources indicate that boozer's raw stats aren't as good as Lendeborg's or even Acuff's, but his impact goes well beyond the box score. His feel for the game is elite for a 19-year-old. Boozer keeps getting better and better as a processor as he continues to log more minutes. The Grizzlies have been one of the league's surprising teams this season. Boozer deserves a ton of credit for that. He wins everywhere he goes, whether at the high school, college, or professional level.

    Acuff just turned 20 last week. In 13 games as a teenager, he averaged 25.5 points per game and became the first teenager in NBA history to score at least 275 points and dish out 80 assists in his first 11 games. Acuff is a special offensive talent who is being asked to do more than any rookie in his class. Sacramento is a very bad basketball team, but Acuff makes the Kings somewhat fun to watch. That's a huge credit to him.

    It has been revealed that the Jazz have been decimated by injuries this season and are currently riding a 12-game losing streak. The one bright side amidst some very bad basketball is how good Peterson has been during that stretch. Peterson had a five-game stretch in which he scored 20 points in each game and shot the ball well from 3. Peterson is the future of Utah's franchise, so getting him as many reps as possible on and off the ball should be the priority.

    Dybantsa, the No. 1 overall pick, is averaging 14 shot attempts per game during his first 10 appearances as a pro. He should be taking even more shots. The way the Wizards are using him is confusing at times. Dybantsa is in somewhat of a weird situation because of the Wizards' roster. Washington handed Trae Young a huge contract this offseason that is already aging poorly. Dybantsa should be the focus of the offense. He should be touching the ball and shooting it even more than he is already. I have been impressed with Dybantsa's defense this season.

    • Bauers, 31, broke out with the World Series champion Milwaukee Brewers this past season, authoring a .266/.389/.484 batting line with 26 home runs that more than doubled his previous career high (12).
    • The Red Sox desperately needed a power bat and certainly added one with Bauers.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Boston Red Sox have made the offseason's first major free agent signing. The Red Sox and first baseman Jake Bauers have agreed to a four-year contract worth a reported $58 million, the team announced on Tuesday.

    Bauers, 31, broke out with the World Series champion Milwaukee Brewers this past season, authoring a .266/.389/.484 batting line with 26 home runs that more than doubled his previous career high (12). He was named the NLCS MVP during Milwaukee's title run thanks to a 4 for 14 (.286) effort. Bauers drove in seven runs in the four-game sweep of the Los Angeles Dodgers.

    The Red Sox desperately needed a power bat and certainly added one with Bauers. Their 163 home runs this past season were the fifth fewest in baseball and three players -- Wilyer Abreu, Willson Contreras and Jarren Duran -- accounted for 71 of those 163 home runs. Boston's lineup figures to look something like this with Bauers now added:.

    In a recent development, that leaves Duran without a full-time position and makes a trade or even a non-tender more likely. Franklin Arias, one of the very best prospects in the minors, could debut early next season and wrestle the shortstop job away from Story. POBO Craig Breslow recently noted Story is not locked in as the team's starting shortstop.

    We ranked Bauers as the 12th-best free agent available this offseason, and the seventh-best position player free agent. Here's our write-up:.

    According to recent reports, rake Bauers (finally) lived up to the nickname this year and carried it over into the postseason, particularly during the NLCS. Long an exit velocity and hard-hit rate darling, Bauers fully tapped into his power in 2026 thanks to a more open stance and moving back in the box and further off the plate. That allowed him to see the ball better and get his bat into the hitting position on time more consistently. I'm not 100% sold on those adjustments solving his career-long problems with lefties, though at least there is a tangible reason to believe in his great left-on-left performance this season. Bauers can be an adventure in the field (he has played outfield in the past) and he just turned 31. A few teams will look for the next Jake Bauers rather than pay the actual Jake Bauers.

    According to recent reports, the Brewers tendered Bauers the $23.15 million qualifying offer and will receive a 2027 compensation draft pick after the first round because the contract exceeds $50 million. Because they paid the competitive balance tax, the Red Sox will forfeit their second- and fifth-highest 2027 draft picks, plus $1 million in bonus pool money for the 2027 international signing period, to sign Bauers.

    Milwaukee could turn to Tyler Black and Andrew Vaughn at first base next season. Andrew Fischer, the No. 20 overall pick in the 2025 draft, slugged 48 home runs in the minors this summer and reached Double-A. He is the long-term solution at first base but is likely a year away from the major leagues. The Brewers could bring in a stopgap first baseman if they're not sold on Black.

    Industry observers note that the Red Sox went 87-75 this past season and were the second wild card team. They were swept by the rival Upcoming York Yankees in the Wild Card Series and scored only two runs in the two games.

    The Philadelphia 76ers are off to a fantastic start to the 2026-27 season at 12-3, good for first in the Eastern Conference, and perhaps most encouraging for the Sixers is that they're winning without looking like a team playing at its absolute peak.

    Recent findings suggest that after a huge offseason adding LeBron James and Jaylen Brown, the Sixers still look like a team figuring out how best to work together, but when it comes time in the fourth quarter to find a way to win, they manage to get the job done. Tyrese Maxey is leading the way with Brown quickly finding his rhythm, but James and Joel Embiid in particular still seem to be feeling it out early in the season.

    James, who has never averaged less than 20.9 points per game in his previous 23 seasons, is averaging just 15.1 points per game and his 44.3/22.5/71.7 shooting splits are all career lows or close to it. As James figures things out, ESPN reported that a Sixers source claimed James "asked coaches to be patient with him as he expects to find his rhythm and get his conditioning in line by December as he ramps up.".

    That report hit social media and caught James' attention, with the 41-year-old star denying ever saying that.

    ESPN didn't report a direct quote from James, and it's very possible the Sixers source offered an anecdote that paraphrased James and used the word patience when James never did. That then ended up on a social media graphic and prompted James to shoot it down.

    What's fascinating here is it's not a scathing report or even anything particularly juicy. James is struggling with his shot early in the year and seems to be figuring out exactly where he fits in the offense alongside Maxey, Brown and Embiid as a scorer. He's still doing plenty of things well -- including leading the team with 6.9 assists per game and just took over third all-time in assists in NBA history -- and the Sixers are still winning even with James ice cold with his jumper, which history suggests will turn around at some point.

    Patience would be prudent from the Sixers with James, whether he wants to use that word or not, and it seems like a matter of when, not if, he gets shots to start falling and the Philly offense becomes even more dynamic.

    #3235. Yankees' David Bednar, Twins' Ryan Jeffers accept qualifying offer, six others reject $23.15 million QO

    📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (788 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy 📈 Bullish 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Yankees' David Bednar, Twins' Ryan Jeffers accept qualifying offer, six others reject $23.15 million QO

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (788 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, two players have accepted this year's one-year, $23.15 million qualifying offer prior to Tuesday's 4 p.m.
    • In a recent development, an eighth free agent, Jake Bauers, also received the QO.
    • In a recent development, the five unsigned free agents who rejected the QO are now tied to draft pick compensation.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, two players have accepted this year's one-year, $23.15 million qualifying offer prior to Tuesday's 4 p.m. ET. deadline, and six others have declined the QO. David Bednar (Yankees) and Ryan Jeffers (Twins) are returning to their teams, for the 2027 season, while Randy Arozarena (Mariners),  Brandon Lowe (Pirates), Adrian Morejon (Padres), Trevor Rogers (Orioles), and Seiya Suzuki (Cubs) are all hitting the market.

    In a recent development, an eighth free agent, Jake Bauers, also received the QO. He agreed to a four-year, $58 million contract with the Red Sox this past weekend. Effectively, Bauers declined the QO. Because they paid CBT in 2026, the Red Sox will surrender their second- and fifth-highest 2027 draft picks, plus $1 million in 2027 international bonus pool money, to sign Bauers. The Brewers, as a revenue-sharing receiver, will receive a compensation draft pick after the first round because the contract exceeds $50 million.

    In a recent development, the five unsigned free agents who rejected the QO are now tied to draft pick compensation. Their former teams will receive a draft pick if they sign elsewhere, and their new teams will be docked a draft pick and potentially international bonus pool money to sign them. The exact compensation depends on the team's revenue sharing and competitive balance tax (CBT) status.

    Here is draft pick compensation the former teams will receive if the seven qualified free agents change teams:.

    Pick after competitive balance round B (before third round) if contract under $50M; pick after first round if over $50M.

    Pick after competitive balance round B (before third round) if contract under $50M; pick after first round if over $50M.

    Pick after competitive balance round B (before third round) if contract under $50M; pick after first round if over $50M.

    Industry observers note that CBT payors, like the Red Sox, will forfeit their second- and fifth-highest 2027 draft picks, plus $1 million in 2027 international bonus pool money, to sign a qualified free agent. Teams that receive revenue sharing will surrender their third-highest 2027 draft pick. All other teams will surrender their second-highest 2027 draft pick and $500,000 in 2027 international bonus pool money.

    It must be noted that declining the QO does not mean the free agent can not return to his former team. The two sides could still work out a contract of any size and any length, including one worth less than QO, though that is very unlikely. Zac Gallen, Michael King, and Kyle Schwarber rejected the QO last offseason and then later re-signed with their teams.

    Free agents must meet certain criteria to be eligible for the QO. Players cannot have received the QO previously and they must have spent the most recent season with one team, meaning anyone traded in-season is ineligible. The Dodgers could not give Tarik Skubal, far and away the offseason's best free agent, the QO following his midseason acquisition.

    The QO is set at the average of the top 125 salaries in the most recent season and that is salaries only, not total compensation. For example, the Yankees paid Cody Bellinger a $20 million signing bonus and a $32.5 million salary in 2026. Only the $32.5 million counts toward the QO calculation. This QO was worth a record $23.15 million this winter.

    Recent findings suggest that the current QO system replaced the old free-agent arbitration system in 2012 and will remain in effect this offseason. The upcoming collective bargaining agreement could change the QO system, if not eliminate it entirely. Entering the offseason, just 18 of the 157 free agents to receive the QO accepted it. That count is now at 20 of 165.

    Recent findings suggest that one of the more effective closers in baseball last season, Bednar closed down 35 of 39 save chances with a 2.47 ERA, 1.04 WHIP and 76 strikeouts in 69 ⅓ innings. Having him back on board means the Yankees don't need to find a fresh closer and can look instead to shore up the bridge to the ninth as needed.

    It has been revealed that there had been talk that Jeffers wanted to stay with the Twins but that he'd decline the QO and then negotiate a long-term deal. There's still room to reach an extension, of course, but he now doesn't have any leverage from outside offers. It's a massive win for the Twins, with Jeffers resuming his role as the everyday catcher and Victor Caratini serving as the primary backup.

    Jeffers hit .256/.353/.461 (127 OPS+) with 14 homers and 56 RBI is only 92 games last season. He's been one of the most productive offensive catchers in baseball over the course of the last four seasons, when healthy.

    Vikings have a secret weapon to fight altitude heading into showdown with 49ers in Mexico City

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (907 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • When the Minnesota Vikings head to Mexico City this week, they'll face multiple challenges, including one they've never really dealt with: altitude.
    • Industry observers note that the Vikings' showdown with the 49ers on Sunday night will take place at Estadio Azteca, which sits at an elevation of just over 7,350 feet.
    • Recent findings suggest that to get acclimated to the altitude, the 49ers are spending their week of practice in Colorado Springs, where the elevation is over 6,600 feet.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    When the Minnesota Vikings head to Mexico City this week, they'll face multiple challenges, including one they've never really dealt with: altitude.

    Industry observers note that the Vikings' showdown with the 49ers on Sunday night will take place at Estadio Azteca, which sits at an elevation of just over 7,350 feet. To put that in perspective, that's more than 2,000 feet higher than the altitude in Denver, which has the highest elevation of any NFL city at 5,280 feet.

    Recent findings suggest that to get acclimated to the altitude, the 49ers are spending their week of practice in Colorado Springs, where the elevation is over 6,600 feet. On the Vikings' end, they've spent the week at their normal practice facility, but they do have a secret weapon that will help them acclimate to the high elevation: The team has been using what is essentially an altitude chamber for the past few weeks.

    Rather than leaving Minnesota to train at altitude before Sunday night’s game in Mexico City, the Vikings built an altitude chamber in Eagan, where players can get familiar with the effects of working in thinner air before Sunday’s game at 7,200 feet (photos courtesy of the… pic.twitter.com/b9FWMF3KxJ.

    The room is full of exercise equipment — like stationary bikes and treadmills — and it lets players simulate training at altitudes up to 12,000 feet. So while they aren't fully practicing in those conditions, they are working out and, they hope, slowly getting their bodies ready.

    The Vikings did give some thought to relocating for the week, but in the end, the team didn't want to take the players out of their normal routine, according to Vikings Vice President of Player Health and Performance, Tyler Williams.

    "As much as they enjoy prime-time games, they love that Sunday-to-Sunday weekly rhythm, and there's so many things now that players take in on nutrition and body work and all their recovery processes and what they do to prepare," Williams stated, via the Vikings official website. "They like their Mondays being their Mondays. We're rhythm-and-process-habit people. And so, knowing that we can reduce [those variables] by staying here, that went into the equation.".

    It has been revealed that when you're at a higher elevation, each breath takes in fewer oxygen molecules, which is why athletes get winded faster when playing at these altitudes. That science is why the Vikings felt the addition of the chamber was necessary.

    "A couple things that [it] looks to achieve: Even though you're not doing a full practice at altitude, you're trying to gain a lower rate of perceived exertion," Williams mentioned.

    According to recent reports, was fascinating to hear #Vikings VP of health & performance Tyler Williams speak about preparing the team for Sunday's game in Mexico City at an altitude of 7,352 feet. Process includes this temporary altitude room at TCO. Players have spent time in there going back many weeks. pic.twitter.com/9t12eM5l1d.

    The Vikings installed the chamber more than five weeks ago, and since then, the players have been taking advantage of it in the facility.

    Sources indicate that "I'd say to date, we have close to 450 sessions accumulated in there," Williams stated. "Nearly our whole roster has done five-plus sessions and nearly our whole roster has [experienced] 12,000 feet, which is great.".

    The team's goal is simple: The Vikings want every player on the roster to be at least somewhat acclimated to the altitude once they land in Mexico City.

    "The more often you're exposed to that, you have a lower rate of perceived exertion," Williams noted. "You also have a behavioral adaptation — how your body responds to [altitude]; how you know how to pace yourself at altitude; how you know how to breathe and use breathing strategies in your first exposure compared to your fifth is totally different. It's a learned adaptation.".

    If you're wondering whether the players like the chamber, the answer seems to be yes, at least according to Justin Jefferson.

    In a recent development, "It's been really good," Jefferson stated of the chamber this week. "It's good to have that feel and to kind of get acclimated to that feeling of being in that altitude. For the past four or five weeks we've been training in there, trying to get our lungs acclimated to taking that. It's different for sure. It's different than what we're really used to, but I feel like we're ready, and they got us well prepared to play fast and play freely and not really [be] thinking about all the extra stuff that goes into it.

    Industry observers note that although this should help the Vikings, they won't be quite as acclimated as San Francisco. With the 49ers spending the week in Colorado, they'll be eating, sleeping and practicing at the higher altitude 24 hours a day, which should fully acclimate their body. On the other hand, the Vikings are only using the chamber for workouts — they're not practicing in it — so it's not quite the same as being fully immersed in a higher altitude like the 49ers.

    According to scientific research, it generally takes one to three days to fully adjust to a higher altitude, but the Vikings won't have that time since they'll be arriving in Mexico City on Saturday. The Vikings are clearly hoping that the altitude chamber will help them adjust just enough to pull out a win in this huge NFC showdown.

    💡 Key Takeaways
