    Access, Not Chances: How Como Took Manchester United Apart – LC

    📅 24 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 21 min read (4238 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Spielverlagerung

    ⏱️ ~21 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • von Next Generation am 24.10.2026 in den Kategorien Champions League,Uncategorized mit 0 Kommentaren.
    • According to recent reports, como beat Manchester United 4-1 — and in this case the scoreline really is a fair expression of the game.
    • Cesc Fàbregas’s side showed two things that rarely go together.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    von Next Generation am 24.10.2026 in den Kategorien Champions League,Uncategorized mit 0 Kommentaren.

    According to recent reports, como beat Manchester United 4-1 — and in this case the scoreline really is a fair expression of the game. For long stretches the match was one-sided, not in terms of chance volume but in terms of access: Como dictated in every phase where the ball went, who received it, and under what conditions it had to be played on. United never got on terms in any of those phases.

    Cesc Fàbregas’s side showed two things that rarely go together. Out of possession, a pressing structure with clear direction, isolation of one side, and man-marking that applied near the ball only for the action in progress while everything around it was already speculating on the second ball. And in possession, a positional game of remarkable technical maturity that ties opponents in, switches play, and works systematically into the space behind them. The 4-1 is therefore less an outlier than evidence of work that has been built up over recent seasons.

    This analysis goes through the phases one by one: first Como in possession and United’s response, then the work against the ball from the high press to defending the box, and finally the goals.

    In build-up, Como moved away from their nominal 4-2-3-1 and sat closer to a 4-3-3, with the eights as the real variable: very free in their movement and above all active in the half-spaces. The base structure stayed stable — a flat four plus a six in front of them, sometimes ahead of the line, sometimes slightly behind the forward line.

    According to recent reports, close to their own goal, Como consistently involved goalkeeper Butez as an additional central player in the build-up. That created a five-against-four against United’s front line — awkward on paper, more awkward still in execution, because Como didn’t use the overload to play through but to tie opponents in. From there, the same shape kept appearing on both the right and the left: centre-back, full-back, a player from the half-position in the eight space, and a six alongside. A diamond that wasn’t an end in itself but had a purpose: the diagonal route out.

    Como’s build-up structure. From a 4-1 (flat four), the half-positions with Paz and Perrone are added. Small triangles and diamonds emerge. The three attackers ahead of them create additional options in behind.

    One detail deserves particular attention. At times the full-backs stood not wide but flat, in a half-position. That sounds like a nuance, but it had a clear function: it vacated the wing and created the space the eights could drop into — Paz and Perrone did so regularly. If you don’t occupy the wing yourself, you force the opponent to guard it anyway.

    ManU got no access near the ball and left large diagonal spaces open on the far side.

    Sources indicate that for United’s midfielders this was close to unsolvable. Tielemans, Mount and Andrey Santos spent the whole game struggling to establish any responsibility at all, let alone get into duels. When an eight dropped out, they couldn’t follow, and if one of them was tied in by it, a two-against-one opened up on the far wing. Como didn’t create that situation once; they created it serially.

    The decisive mechanism lay in receiving and relaying the ball. The player in the deeper position usually worked with two touches: the first took the ball backwards, the second relayed it to the free teammate. At the end of every one of those actions stood a player with the game in front of him — and from that open position he could switch play.

    Industry observers note that what made it possible were the preparatory movements. Paz and captain Da Cunha first lured their markers in the wrong direction and then worked with the head start they’d bought. That head start isn’t only space, it’s above all time: time to control the ball first and relay it second, rather than having to do both in one touch.

    Industry observers note that A scene in the 17th minute is typical. Mason Mount steps out, Mazraoui goes into the duel at the same time — nominally United are in an overload here. Only neither of them really gets to the opponent, because both are too late. Paz can therefore calmly take his touch backwards and switch play directly with the second, dissolving the pressure before it had even formed.

    It has been revealed that when the build-up ran down the right, it showed in a recurring pattern: Paz and Da Cunha took the first touch backwards or inside and then switched with the left foot out of a closed body position. The players they found were systematically in open positions — Milla, the far-side six, or the wing-to-wing connection directly.

    In the second half, Como adjusted the shape and more often played with two sixes, to form the diamonds faster and switch to the far-side six faster. Couto stood out in this: the right-back repeatedly played the chip into the six or ten space — six or seven times in a row during one spell. It was mainly Paz who received the ball there and could launch the attack.

    In the second half Como focus on those diagonal spaces and look for them mainly with chipped balls.

    It has been revealed that especially striking inside the diamond are the rotations between the players. Because of the connections between them, they moved in rotation depending on running path, space and ball movement. The same recurring spaces were re-occupied. Under pressure on the ball carrier, the outer players pushed flat or ran in behind the opponents; the highest player in the diamond burst out of the cover shadow and became the reference point in depth. On a deep pass, the two wide players released and joined the depth, able to offer themselves again immediately in an open body position. If the pass went via the flat wide players, the spaces in front of the new ball carrier could be run into. Every rotation, every positional adjustment was coordinated with the others and, in the end, produced a stream of pressure-resolving passes while Manchester United chased the press in vain.

    Industry observers note that como bridged the middle third exceptionally swiftly, via dribbles at speed and diagonal passes. Behind it stood a recognisable principle: first tie the opponent to one wing, then get behind them via the diagonal, and in the final third do the same thing again. In sum, that produced the shape of a Z — build-up on the right, transition on the left, finish from the right again.

    In this example Como pin ManU in the press with their short passing. Thanks to the extra attacker on the ball-near side they can play through the pressure and switch.

    The connections between wingers and striker carried these attacks and were deliberately kept flexible. The wide players sometimes stayed wide, sometimes came short, sometimes tucked inside. Douvikas accordingly either waited deep in front of the line for the chipped ball or, when space opened up on the wing, received the deeper pass and then ran in behind along the wing as soon as the ball sat on the full-back’s open foot. That flexibility produced the overloads on one side, and the overloads produced the central overload.

    Recent findings suggest that in the final third one element was added that is rare in fast transition teams: patience. Como drew opponents towards them with dribbles and short passes, used back-passes when needed, and then switched in front of the block. Da Cunha, Baturina and Paz were the three who could tie opponents in and then find the diagonal. They created the positions on the diagonal, were available to receive, and used their space to apply pressure. The block was usually tied in with short touches, the switch and the position behind the opponent prepared, and quick finishes sought.

    The intensity in possession shouldn’t be underestimated. Practically every attack involved at least three or four players, the width was occupied, the centre likewise, and there were multiple options throughout. What they looked for almost every time was the space behind the opponent on the far side — exactly the zone that is closed last when a block shifts across.

    Industry observers note that paz brought the right profile for this pattern. A strong left foot cutting inside from the right, he repeatedly dropped into the right-hand blind side of his opponents, got shots away there with few touches, and racked up the most shots of the match. That the finishes generally came off few touches isn’t a detail but the consequence of the time won further back.

    In a recent development, as the move continues, Como again look for the blind side of the defenders. Here Douvikas and Paz are positioned in behind, with Da Cunha joining in front of the back line. After briefly pinning the opponents, the switch reaches Da Cunha, who misses the target from distance.

    Recent findings suggest that what carries all of this is the technical execution. Soft passes, sharp ones when the moment called for it, consistently well timed and played into the right foot — for ninety minutes. Passing that secure at that tempo is what makes a variable concept actually retrievable.

    According to recent reports, united’s basic problem out of possession was the hybrid. They pressed half man-oriented, but with a plus-one in the last line — a construction that forces compromises in both directions. It demands access up front that it doesn’t fund at the back.

    There were certainly moments when it worked. When Dalot pushed through into the press on the right and passed his man backwards, a clean man-orientation emerged all the way up to the front — and with it a clear assignment for Mount, out of which the ball could be won. But that stayed the exception. Most of the time Dalot sat too flat out of possession, so United couldn’t trigger the duels up front and went into the press a man short.

    Sources indicate that mount was the most conspicuous case in this respect. He barely got into a duel across the whole match because the decision to step out always came too late. Against a team that works with preparatory movements, a late decision is practically the same as none: the opponent already has the head start before the journey even begins.

    Recent findings suggest that on top of that came a problem on the far side. There, United’s winger frequently failed to protect the depth — usually Mbeumo, who jogged back rather than closing the space. But that was precisely the target zone of Como’s diagonal switches. It allowed them to change sides almost at will and regularly find an open structure on the other side.

    The second half brought no improvement. The distances to opponents stayed large, and centrally what was actually intended still didn’t materialise. Michael Carrick’s double change at half-time was meant to bring more physicality to the six with Carlos Baleba, but it didn’t solve the problem — the assignments still didn’t work, the duels in the centre still didn’t happen, and the wide positions dragged the eights out further, which opened latest spaces.

    In the end the energy simply wasn’t there to press with the necessary intensity. United’s press became increasingly static, and a static press against an opponent with this passing quality yields not a single ball win — it only hands them the starting positions they’re looking for anyway.

    Como started the game in a high press and sustained it above all in the first half, with isolated spells after the break too. It was triggered on back-passes and goal kicks — and, remarkably, by their own goals: after every strike the team immediately pushed high again instead of managing the lead in a deeper block.

    In a recent development, the steering ran consistently towards United’s left build-up side. The reason is personnel: Harry Maguire played there with his weaker left foot as the outside foot, and next to him stood another right-footer in Noussair Mazraoui on the left. Two right-footers on one build-up side means the ball always has to be taken back inside to play on — exactly where Como were closing the door. The press was usually triggered by the left-sided forward, with the ball ending up at either Maguire or Mazraoui.

    Pressing structure after the change in the second half.

    Recent findings suggest that in the centre Como defended man-oriented, with both sixes pushing very high and taking flat passes into United’s midfielders out of the game. That removed the short route through the middle as an option and left the long ball. But the long ball triggered nothing for United: the second balls went to Como practically every time.

    According to recent reports, that isn’t chance, it’s running work. The sixes consistently tracked the negative pressing paths back, anticipated the long ball early, and were in front of the line before it arrived. Luis Milla covered the most ground of any player on the pitch in this pattern — recovery runs after being played past, doubling up on the ball, attacking the second ball. When the long ball came from Maguire or one of the full-backs, a six was regularly in front of the line with an intense sprint, sealing the centre, taking away the diagonal follow-up passes and attacking the loose balls.

    Defending the long ball and extra support on the second ball.

    In a recent development, once the ball was on one side, that side was isolated. The near-side forward had access to the centre-back and dropped back a touch when the pass went to the full-back, so that he covered centre-back and six simultaneously and closed the square pass. The far-side forward marked the goalkeeper. That served two functions at once: it took away United’s escape route via the keeper along with the switch, and it kept a player in position for the moment of the turnover.

    Industry observers note that the double pivot worked in a deliberate half-position. The near-side six stayed tight to his man, the far-side one dropped slightly behind him — securing the space and at the same time establishing access to the far-side centre-back in United’s back three.

    In a recent development, the last line defended largely man-for-man in the high press, and very tightly. But the decisive detail is the one that carries the whole concept: the man-marking near the ball applied only to the action in progress. Around it, players were already releasing from their assignments and orienting towards the second ball. That is only retrievable at very high intensity — and it’s the reason United’s forced long balls produced not a single usable moment.

    Industry observers note that when Como dropped a line, the man-orientation at the second height stayed exceptionally high. Here too the back-pass served as the trigger to push up as a unit and tip back into man-marking. If United were in a closed body position, the Comaschi had already pushed up far enough to attack the back-pass at the moment it was played — a pattern that led directly to the 3-0. The half-position was at work there again: closing down level with the centre-back while simultaneously prepared to push through onto the next player deeper.

    Recent findings suggest that in the first half Como still had problems assigning the half-positions against ManU’s 3-2-5. In this example Fernandes moves to the wing, Como fail to establish responsibility and access and are played through at mid-height.

    Up to half-time, though, Como had a structural problem with this. The pure man-marking didn’t come off cleanly, because of the two sixes in front of the line, one should really have tucked in and taken over the half-position for the centre-backs. That didn’t happen consistently. The consequence: a centre-back stepped out, the space behind him stayed unoccupied, and that was exactly what United kept attacking.

    It has been revealed that the pattern of pressing onto Manchester United’s left side continued in the second half, now with Dalot at full-back. The press was still triggered by Douvikas, with the ball-near winger pushing up as a second striker to press the centre-back. Paz focused on the visitors’ ball-near six and Couto pushed through onto Dalot. Through the central connections the game was isolated on one side.

    Recent findings suggest that at half-time Como adjusted. One six moved directly into the line, with the far-side winger pushing in onto the six — they now pressed out of a 5-2-1-2. Lucas Da Cunha pressed through from the right onto Maguire, while Nico Paz picked up United’s six. The central forward pressed the central centre-back and from there carried on to the goalkeeper. The far-side wide midfielder and the remaining six were poised — one onto United’s free six, one onto the far-side centre-back — again in that half-position between opponent and the space to be protected.

    ManU building up high against the man-oriented Italians.

    According to recent reports, the effect was immediately visible. Como controlled the half-positions, got access right into the last line throughout, and set the rhythm of the match from then on. The adjustment solved exactly the problem the first half had left open, without changing the underlying principle.

    In the final phase Como defended from a very deep line inside the box. That left barely any space behind the line to play into — which United hardly looked for anyway. The visitors attacked little depth and rarely occupied the width in the final third, so Como could stay compact without being punished for it.

    Sources indicate that accordingly, a lot of players stood very centrally in and in front of the box. That produced numerous cover shadows and a numerical superiority around the ball, which allowed them to steer actively within the block rather than merely react. At times they deliberately steered inside, to guide the opponent into the prepared congestion and cover from a deeper position.

    Deep back line in the box, centre closed and play steered inside. The box defending allowed the English side shots from distance.

    It has been revealed that the crucial point is that Como left the gaps open not despite this set-up but because of it. If you pack the box and secure the depth, you give up the space in front of the line — and that is exactly where United were supposed to shoot from.

    The numbers vindicate the decision. Taking the conceded goal out of the box, Como allowed nine shots from outside the penalty area across ninety minutes, worth roughly 0.24 xG combined; only three of them were even on target. On top of that, of the four shots inside the box, two came from at least 14 to 15 metres and effectively belong in the long-range category as well. United accepted the invitation, and the shooting quality was perfectly decent — it’s just that with that scoring probability over a whole match, the most likely outcome is precisely what happened.

    Tracking the ball for the first goal.

    1-0, Nico Paz (2′) — The goal comes before United are even set. Como take the goal kick promptly and play straight to the full-back, luring the visitors into the press — only not cleanly. Mason Mount triggers the pressure and is played past, and on the second ball he goes into the duel as well instead of holding the middle and looking for the space where he could pick the ball up. That is exactly what opens the centre, the space for the second ball is there, and Paz can play it through.

    What follows is the transition principle in its purest form: a quick switch to the diagonal side, then short passes against a very deep line. Matheus Cunha doesn’t pick up the player behind him and leaves the ten space open, where Paz is standing. He needs two touches because neither Cunha from above nor Maguire from his distance gets into the duel. Lammens, for his part, doesn’t defend the goal with his cover shadow but takes the near post — which leaves the far corner to a strong left foot. The curled finish into it is quality, though.

    It has been revealed that 2-0, Anastasios Douvikas (49′, assist Paz) — Same zone, same cause. Bryan Mbeumo doesn’t choose to shut the centre but closes the centre-back, which creates the space for Da Cunha, who drives forward and plays Martin Baturina in. Centrally, Mount again fails to pick up his man. Out wide, Amad Diallo, introduced at half-time, generates no pressure centrally, so Mazraoui can’t take over the deep wide player in the first place.

    The result is Paz behind the opponent, in the ten space, dribbling unopposed at goal. Matthijs de Ligt establishes no reference to Douvikas’s run in behind and slips as well — a one-against-one with the goalkeeper that Douvikas finishes coolly.

    3-0, Nico Paz (57′) — The only goal that comes directly out of the work against the ball. Como are in the midfield press in a closed position with access to the inside lane, win the ball there and punish a lapse of concentration in the visitors’ build-up. At the end, Paz is alone in front of Lammens again.

    4-0, Jacobo Ramón (76′, assist Kaiki) — This goal comes from a longer possession spell and indicates the assignment problem in its clearest form. Mazraoui is too narrow and has no access to the wide player. Diallo stands in the space with access to neither the central player nor the full-back nor the winger — an orientation that doesn’t work in any direction.

    Industry observers note that como switch to Máximo Perrone, who can slide the ball out wide because the space is simply free. From there comes the cross from an open body position, and in the centre Como run a two-against-one at the end of which Ramón scores.

    According to recent reports, 4-1, Joshua Zirkzee (90′) — Como’s only lapse, and one in a phase in which the team had already dropped very deep. United get the ball to the wing, it’s two against two in the box, and the cross is initially only feinted. Zirkzee orients himself well forwards at that moment, while Como’s defenders are already stepping out after the feinted cross. Diallo’s ball in behind the line is strong, the offside call is razor-thin in his favour, and Zirkzee takes two touches before finishing one-against-one with the goalkeeper. A blemish, not a structural problem.

    According to recent reports, the common denominator — Three of Como’s four goals come in the same zone: the space in front of and behind United’s line that nobody takes responsibility for. Mount is involved in two of those scenes through an assignment he never establishes, Diallo in two more after coming on. Nico Paz is at the heart of three of the four goals, twice as scorer, once as the provider — always out of the opponent’s blind side.

    Como’s 4-1 has one common cause across every phase, and it lies less in any single idea than in its execution under continuous load. Out of possession they steered, isolated and speculated on the second ball — with man-marking that applied near the ball only for the action in progress and was already dissolved around it. In possession they tied opponents in, switched play and worked systematically into the space behind. Both require eleven players to anticipate a teammate’s decision, and both functioned over the full distance.

    Industry observers note that the connecting detail is the half-position. In the press, the far-side six stood between opponent and the space to be protected; in possession, the eights worked out of the same zone, and the full-backs occupied it flat in order to vacate the wing for exactly those players. Como, in other words, occupied the position in both directions from which two jobs can be done at once — which is why the side could neither be played past in the press nor be pinned in the build-up.

    Industry observers note that for United the diagnosis is more uncomfortable than the result. The problem wasn’t individual errors but that the team never, in any phase, got into the duels it needed. The mixture of half man-orientation and a plus-one in the last line funded no access up front, and without access every decision is made too late — from Mount in the centre to Mbeumo failing to secure the far-side depth. Carrick’s double change at half-time was meant to bring physicality to the six with Carlos Baleba, but it changed nothing about the assignments, and in Diallo a player came on wide who reached neither one opponent nor the other in his space. That the energy ran out in the end was a consequence rather than a cause.

    That leaves the context. A 4-1 against Manchester United is no proof in itself, and Como’s finishing was exceptionally efficient on the night. What showed regardless of the result, though, is a team with a recognisable, rehearsed answer in all four phases of the game — and one that put a technical maturity on the pitch in possession that you wouldn’t readily credit to a side promoted two years ago.

    See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results.

    PSV Eindhoven endured a frustrating night in the Champions League as their defensive frailties were exposed in a 2-1 defeat by Club Brugge.

    PSV started full of attacking intent and should have taken an early lead when Ivan Perisic put Sergiño Dest clean through on goal, but the defender’s shot was too close to goalkeeper Yann Sommer.

    Instead it was the visitors who took the lead with their first real attack when Nicolo Tresoldi headed in a teasing cross from Joaquin Seys.

    According to recent reports, PSV equalised early in the second half as an outstanding pass by Sven Mijnans into the path Lutsharel Geertruida allowed the defender to charge to the byline. His pullback found its way to Kodai Sano, whose shot took a deflection off Seys into the net.

    But five minutes later PSV were caught out as another razor-sharp pass by Seys released Carlos Forbs in space to net the winner.

    The home side refused to give up, but were unable to find a way past Sommer in the closing stages as the Belgian side closed out the win.

    Industry observers note that team captain Mauro Junior admitted that PSV had been undone by shortcomings at the back. “We had a lot of opportunities in the first half but we didn’t score,” he told Ziggo Sport.

    Sources indicate that “We want to attack and score goals, but we weren’ well organised today in defence. We need to keep our heads up and look forward to the next game.”.

    The result leaves PSV in 24th place, just above the elimination line, ahead of their next match away to Real Madrid on November 24, with four points from their opening four matches.

    Arsenal will host old nemesis José Mourinho’s Real Madrid in the league phase of the Champions League.

    Mourinho, the former Chelsea, Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur manager, will return to London to resume hostilities against last season’s beaten finalists.

    During his two spells as Chelsea manager, Mourinho famously had run-ins with Arsenal’s Arsène Wenger.

    Mourinho called Wenger a “specialist in failure” after the Frenchman failed to add to his three Premier League titles following his Portuguese counterpart’s arrival in London in 2004.

    Last season, Mikel Arteta finally ended Arsenal’s long wait to be crowned champions of England but agonisingly missed out on European glory.

    Industry observers note that verdict Premier League champions should not be daunted by any game, but Real Madrid – with Mourinho in control – has the feel of a defining match of the group stage.     Sources indicate that that brings our coverage of the Champions League draw to an end, as the 36 teams found which eight teams they will be facing in the league phase of this season’s tournament. Thanks for joining us!

    This season is the third under the upcoming format, with a league phase instead of a group stage, and Uefa has confirmed that fixtures that have taken place in the league phase of the two previous seasons cannot be repeated this time around.

    Recent findings suggest that administrateur du site web sportif canadien Dans les coulisses, le rappeur et compositeur Maxime Truman a indiqué jeudi dernier que le milliardaire propriétaire de l'ASSE aurait été sondé pour reprendre le Montreal CF (anciennement dénommé Impact de Montréal), ex-club québécois de Patrice Ferri, Idriss Ech Chergui et Ignacio Piatti. Extraits.

    Recent findings suggest that "Geoff Molson aurait eu des discussions avec Larry Tanenbaum afin d'aller voir, ne serait-ce que dans une étape exploratoire, si l'idée d'acheter le CF Montréal (pour le garder à Montréal) a du sens économiquement parlant. Larry Tanenbaum est un Ontarien de 81 ans dont la fortune est évaluée à un peu moins de 3 milliards de dollars américains nets. Il a vendu le mois dernier les parts qu'il détenait dans MLSE pour une société de 4,35 milliards de dollars canadiens, argent qu'il a utilisé pour rembourser des dettes d'investissement et pour sécuriser un peu son patrimoine. Du moins, à court terme….

    It has been revealed that il a joué un rôle déterminant dans l'acquisition des Raptors de Toronto et de l'Air Canada Centre, donnant naissance à l'empire MLSE. Il a agi à titre de gouverneur du comité exécutif pour les Maple Leafs, les Raptors, le Toronto FC et les Argonauts. Il est connu, apprécié et respecté des dirigeants et des autres propriétaires de la MLS. Il a même été élu président du conseil des gouverneurs de la NBA. Tanenbaum possède encore plusieurs entités sportives professionnelles, via sa société Kilmer Sports Venture : Tempo de Toronto (avec Geoff Molson, WNBA), LPHF (il a été le premier investisseur canadien un peu plus tôt cette année) et AS Saint-Étienne (Ligue 2 en France). Il possède aussi la Compagnie d'embouteillage Coca-Cola Canada Limitée (Coca-Cola Canada Bottling).

    La candidature de Larry Tanenbaum n'est toutefois pas parfaite. First, il est un fier Torontois. Il est membre de l'Ontario Sports Hall of Fame et il a fait des dons majeurs dans la Ville Reine, notamment pour lancer l'Institut Tanenbaum des sciences du sport à l'Université de Toronto. Il a encore une équipe à Toronto (Tempo), ce qui rendrait possiblement un investissement à Montréal « discutable » aux yeux de plusieurs Torontois. Mais bon, Geoff Molson a investi à Toronto (Tempo) et on l'aime encore à Montréal… Second, Tanenbaum a retiré ses billes de MLSE pour les réinvestir dans de plus petits projets. Le Tempo lui a coûté 50 millions de dollars américains il y a deux ans et il a payé l'ASSE environ 25 millions d'euros la même année. Bref, il semble désormais privilégier les investissements un peu plus modestes. Third, à 81 ans, on pourrait penser qu'il ne se lancera pas dans d'énormes investissements plutôt risqués. Cependant, son fils Kenneth joue un rôle dirigeant majeur au sein de l'entreprise. Il occupe le poste de VP du conseil d'administration et dirige plusieurs de ses filiales.".

    Désormais âgé de 29 ans, l'ancienne pépite stéphanoise Allan Saint-Maximin a accordé il y a 15 jours un entretien à The Athletic.

    In a recent development, "Le Mexique était l'un des meilleurs endroits où j'ai pu vivre, et ma famille s'y sentait tellement bien. Mais parfois, des choses arrivent et vous n'avez pas le choix. Des choses se sont produites avec mes enfants, pas seulement une fois, mais à plusieurs reprises. Ils ont essayé de les harceler et leur ont dit des choses très blessantes à cause de leur couleur de peau. À cause de cela, c'est devenu un problème majeur. Il faut réagir, il faut prendre une décision et la mienne a été de partir, parce que je ne voulais pas que cela arrive et que mes enfants se disent : "Oh, nous devons accepter ça.

    Mon fils de sept ans, Dayde, a été particulièrement affecté parce qu'il ne comprenait pas l'espagnol aussi bien que ses sœurs, Lyana et Ninhia, et ne comprenait pas pourquoi les gens se moquaient de lui. Il me disait : "Ils rient à cause de mes vêtements". Et il ajoutait : "Non, je ne veux plus porter ça". Quand j'ai compris que c'était à cause de sa couleur de peau, je lui ai dit : "Mon fils, ils ne parlaient pas de tes vêtements, ils parlaient de ta peau. Et ils faisaient des blagues parce que tu n'as pas la même peau qu'eux.

    Recent findings suggest that C'est douloureux. Certaines personnes ne voulaient pas jouer avec lui à cause de ça. "C'est comme ça dans tous les pays, ce n'est pas propre au Mexique. On ne peut pas accepter cela. Si cela s'était produit en France, en Arabie saoudite ou en Amérique, j'aurais pris exactement la même décision. Je devais taper du poing sur la table et prendre cette décision pour ma famille. Après une belle expérience de quelques mois à Lens, je suis heureux à Charlotte. Il n'y a pas de meilleur endroit que l'Amérique pour les enfants, c'est le rêve américain. À chaque fois que j'ouvre mon téléphone, je vois un but incroyable en MLS. Il y a tellement de buts spectaculaires dans cette ligue !

    Le système actuel n'aime pas les joueurs comme moi. C'est un fait. Ils n'aiment pas les joueurs dotés d'une grande qualité de dribble et qui font se lever les supporters. Il faut trouver un équilibre, vous n'êtes pas là juste pour faire des passements de jambes et pénaliser votre équipe. Mais c'est très key de préserver cela. Rayan Cherki, qui évolue à Manchester City, est l'un des joueurs que je préfère regarder. Les supporters viennent au stade pour quoi ? Est-ce qu'ils viennent nous voir faire passe, passe, passe ? Ils ne viennent pas pour ça. Ils viennent pour un joueur comme Lamine Yamal, Kylian Mbappé, Ronaldo, Ronaldinho, Zidane... viennent pour ce genre de joueur. À long terme, si nous continuons à perdre ce type de profil, le football va devenir tellement ennuyeux... Ce n'est pas ce que nous voulons.

    Sources indicate that enfant, je jouais des petits matchs entre amis dans les rues de Meudon, près de Paris. Je jouais dehors tous les jours et c'est ce qui manque un peu aujourd'hui. On ne voit plus beaucoup de jeunes jouer dehors : ils jouent à la PlayStation, restent sur leur téléphone, au lieu d'aller dehors et de jouer au foot toute la journée. À cause de cela, beaucoup de choses commencent à changer. Ce n'est pas seulement à cause des entraîneurs.

    According to recent reports, pour les fans de Premier League, je suis surtout connu pour mes quatre années passées à Newcastle United. J'ai eu des opportunités de quitter ce club plus tôt mais les supporters tes Magpies m'ont tout donné. C'est comme avec vos enfants. Vous préparez tout pour eux. Vous ramassez leur caca, vous nettoyez, vous faites tout ce que vous pouvez. Et quand ils arrivent au sommet, ils vous regardent en disant : "Merci papa, maintenant tu peux t'en aller, je vais vivre ma vie". Non, vous ne pouvez pas trahir comme ça. Ils m'ont tout donné et c'était très crucial d'être loyal.

    It has been revealed that steve Bruce était un entraîneur incroyable, mais nous n'avions pas un effectif incroyable. Je n'oublierai jamais les supporters de Newcastle. Mon souvenir marquant, c'est le 3-3 contre le Manchester City de Pep Guardiola à St James' Park. J'avais délivré deux passes décisives. Quand vous jouez contre une grande équipe, que vous voyez Guardiola au bord du terrain, que vous prenez le ballon, et qu'il met sa main sur sa tête en mode "Mais c'est qui ce joueur ? C'est un cauchemar"..., vous sentez que quelque chose est différent. Entendre le soutien du public quand vous prenez le ballon, le sentir vous pousser... Vous avez l'impression de voler. C'est quelque chose de spécial.

    Un autre moment marquant a été mon but victorieux contre Oxford United lors d'un match rejoué du 4e tour de la FA Cup, et l'incident de la célébration du "péniscoptère" qui a suivi. Alors que je célébrais mon but lors de ce match diffusé en direct sur la BBC, un supporter de Newcastle a été aperçu en train de s'exhiber dans la tribune extérieure. L'incident est devenu viral et a entraîné une enquête policière. C'était fou. C'était incroyable, c'était un match de coupe contre une équipe de League One (D3). Ce sont ce genre de choses qui vous aident à comprendre ce qu'est Newcastle.

    En plus de mon académie, je m'occupe d'Helios, un jeu de cartes inspiré de la mythologie grecque que j'ai créé. J'ai récemment reçu offre de 26 millions d'euros de la part d'une entreprise pour racheter ce jeu gratuit mais je l'ai refusée car je souhaite continuer à le développer lui-même. Tout n'est pas une question d'argent. Le but est de créer quelque chose, de créer des emplois pour les gens, de créer des opportunités. Je préférerais m'associer avec d'autres personnes qui prendraient des parts dans la société en échange de leur investissement.

    Industry observers note that alors que j'ai 29 ans et que je me prépare pour les play-offs de MLS avec Charlotte, quel conseil je donnerais au jeune homme que j'étais ? J'étais moins intelligent qu'aujourd'hui. C'est comme un jeu d'échecs, et j'aime jouer aux échecs. Il faut être malin et utiliser sa tête, pas seulement ses émotions. Je n'ai jamais joué en Ligue des champions mais j'estime que j'aurais mérité une sélection en équipe de France à un moment donné de ma carrière. Je suis heureux de tout ce que j'ai accompli. C'est le problème de l'être humain : toujours vouloir plus et ne pas vraiment apprécier ce qu'il a. Je vais continuer à travailler pour faire encore mieux, mais je suis heureux de ce que j'ai.".

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Rumours of Manchester City’s supposed demise without Pep Guardiola appear to be much exaggerated.
    • Sources indicate that they swept past Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park with a style of play under new manager Enzo Maresca that was just as swashbuckling as under his predecessor, with Rayan Cherki playing the role of chief architect.
    • City created enough space for themselves through clever movement.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Rumours of Manchester City’s supposed demise without Pep Guardiola appear to be much exaggerated.

    Sources indicate that they swept past Crystal Palace at Selhurst Park with a style of play under new manager Enzo Maresca that was just as swashbuckling as under his predecessor, with Rayan Cherki playing the role of chief architect. The Frenchman’s two goals included a captivating mazy dribble, which will long be remembered by those who had the fortune to see it.

    City created enough space for themselves through clever movement. With Cherki zigging one way and Phil Foden zagging the other, they created even more by dribbling past a mesmerised Palace back three that became a back five at times and still could not cope.

    Erling Haaland also scored twice. Even with the creative and unpredictable talents of those behind in a four-man attacking City midfield, Haaland remains irreplaceable with his ability to convert chances.

    It has been revealed that however, this night belonged to Cherki. Guardiola chided him publicly after he set up a City goal with a “rabona” cross last season. The thrust of Guardiola’s comments were that Cherki was not Lionel Messi. Of course not, but he possesses a genius all of his own, which Maresca would surely be foolish to rein in.

    The jaw-dropping splendour of Cherki’s first goal drew a collective intake of breath at Selhurst Park.

    Collecting a Foden pass, he attacked the Palace area on a diagonal path, slaloming between Jaydee Canvot, Takehiro Tomiyasu and Chris Richards, before having the spatial awareness and technique to flick his left foot at the ball to send it rolling on a perpendicular trajectory past Dean Henderson.

    "The man with the magic feet!"Rayan Cherki doubles Manchester City's lead with a STUNNING goal 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/9Zea5vFljv.

    An insight into Cherki’s mindset came after the match.

    He noted: “My performance is s---. In the first half, we didn’t find the space, I played bad. I need to show them that I want to play, I want to score. Next time I want to give the ball around more.”.

    Forget the words, Maresca cannot ignore the actions of a player he left on the bench against Bournemouth.

    Sterner tests will come for City than against a Palace side missing key players who may or may not leave south London in the remaining days of the transfer window.

    Whether Maresca will trust his forward players to express themselves as freely against their rivals for the Premier League title remains to be seen, but with Elliot Anderson providing a one-man shield behind them, City could not be stopped.

    Maresca said: “For sure Rayan is happy tonight. His performance was very good and not just for his two goals. He has to press off the ball and he was in charge of [marking] Adam Wharton, so it was a complete game by him.”.

    Only for the first three minutes did Palace hint at a different outcome but, after shots from Eddie Nketiah and Daichi Kamada were diverted away for corners, City took control.

    They took the lead in the 17th minute when the otherwise quiet Antoine Semenyo flighted a cross over the heads of everyone except the shorn locks of Haaland, whose determined header looped over Henderson and dropped in the far corner.

    The only negative of Foden’s performance came in front of goal, with a ballooned shot and a mistimed header.

    After Cherki’s solo masterpiece had made it 2-0, Yeremy Pino seized the next moment for his own with a stunning free-kick that flicked the crossbar, then the back of City keeper Gianluigi Donnarumma before finally dropping over the line.

    "This is a good a free-kick as you're likely to see this season!" Yéremy Pino's stirke beats Donnarumma 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5uF4vzOXDp.

    Whatever hope that mustered was snatched away again when Cherki scored his second goal and the third goal of a breathless five minutes.

    His shot at the end of a darting run flicked the ankle of Tomiyasu to send it just out of Henderson’s reach.

    Rayan Cherki AGAIN! Manchester City have breathing room once again after another strike from the Frenchman 👏 pic.twitter.com/Tyw9whPS2r.

    Morocco teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi had little time to show why City have paid Lille £85.6m for him with a late entry as a substitute, but they didn’t need him on this occasion.

    Foden then set off on a swerving run that set up Haaland to lash home his second goal of the game and make it 4-1.

    In a recent development, erling Haaland scores gets another! 🔥 pic.twitter.com/4mz2eF7wFF.

    The fear for Palace is that they cannot keep selling their best players and expecting to replicate the success on the pitch that has brought them three trophies in the past 15 months.

    Leicester City offer a shuddering example of that. From Premier League champions to League One in 10 seasons.

    Pierre Sage, the new Palace manager, will welcome the certainty that the closure of the transfer window will bring, particularly over the futures of forwards Ismaïla Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta, as well as wing-back Daniel Muñoz.

    The one player he cannot afford to lose is Wharton, who matched the City midfield on his own at times in the first half.

    Sage mentioned: “I think the score is heavy. We stayed in the game for 65 minutes and created some chances. We know we are in for a tough season, but we have created a lot of opportunities in the first two games.

    Recent findings suggest that “I could speak about the transfer window, but I don’t want to find an excuse. We just have to be sure that in four days’ time, the team will be better than today.”.

    “It has been a short pre-season. Rayan [Cherki], five weeks ago was at the World Cup. Game by game, we will be back, just need a few games. We played well, it is a newly introduced manager but we have been playing together, with the addition of a few new players. We know what to do and have to trust the system.”.

    “We have to keep on playing together, find out where we are best and how to play. We have so many good players and we have to fit everyone in. He has to keep going because we know how good Phil is, it is about showing it week in week out. This is the right step forward for everyone. We have to build on this.”.

    "I'm just trying to play my football" 💪Elliot Anderson is excited about the future at Manchester City after his summer transfer 🔥 pic.twitter.com/huGv4Li3GZ.

It will take Pierre Sage a while to impose his style of play. It will certainly take another week before he knows his final squad for the first half of the season.

    It was noticeable at the final whistle that many Palace fans stayed around to applaud Daniel Munoz, an unused substitute on the night, as he made his way to the tunnel, probably for the final time as a Palace player if Nottingham Forest’s interest in him becomes a transfer by the end of the window.

Cherki’s cross picks out Foden inside the six-yard box and the latter should score but he gets a simple header all wrong.

Even the roar from the enclave of City fans took a moment to fill the south London air. You wouldn’t say that all the pre-match optimism among Palace fans has been punctured, but the home side need a moment if they aren’t to sink without trace to a City side bossing possession and territory now.

    That is a huge miss from Foden. Anderson picks out his compatriot in acres of space on the right side of the box, with no Palace defender within five yards of him, but Foden blazes over the bar when he should have put Manchester City 2-0 up.

    Recent findings suggest that he has barely touched the ball thus far but he puts the visitors ahead just past the quarter-of-an-hour mark.     The first chance of the game goes the way of the hosts. It stems from a quite sensational first-time pass from Wharton from inside his own half into the left channel to pick out the run of Nketiah, whose shot from the left side of the box takes a deflection off Dias and is saved by Donnarumma.

    Manchester City initially clear the corner but Palace keep it alive. Kamada’s shot from just inside the box appeared to be on target but it is headed over for another corner, which is easily caught by Donnarumma.

    We are under way at Selhurst Park. Will Pierre Sage earn his first win as Palace boss or can Enzo Maresca and City make it two wins from two?

And having done so, he fairly skipped up the steps back with his dad back to their seats. Whether the boy’s second wish of the evening, for a Palace victory, will come true is another question altogether.

    The young Palace fan is still waiting for Haaland. Another determined walk back to the dressing room. It isn’t a simple task to attract an opposition player’s attention when you are leaning over a barrier a few feet higher than him – and in the home end. Haaland and his teammates have the look of a team that knows it must perform tonight to ease the concerns that they are a team in transition. The City fans will not entertain such thoughts, either.

    Recent findings suggest that “He is a genius. Make no mistake. Managers now want structure, they do not like players who are a bit loose out of possession. But I go to football matches to watch people like him play.

Some managers will not appreciate it. But last week he got his manager out of a hole because without him they would not have won that game.”.

    Was it really just a year ago when Crystal Palace fans flooded down the Holmesdale Road with not a care in the world having just won the Community Shield to add to their FA Cup triumph over tonight’s opponents Manchester City? Well, they are marching along the Holmesdale Road in the same numbers again this evening, bedecked in red and blue as always, yet there is uncertainty and worry in the air and on their faces. Will the player exodus continue? What should they make of new manager Pierre Sage? Will the good times fade from view as quickly as they did for Leicester City or can Sage build a new side to match the one which, under Oliver Glasner, added the Conference League to their list of trophies three months ago?

    “We struggled to get into the game and win the battles,” a disappointed Carlo Ancelotti lamented.

    At the World Cup, an industrious 18-year-old revealed maturity beyond his years to dominate the midfield against Ancelotti’s Brazil on his competitive international debut, earning Morocco a draw. That was, in fact, the second time an Ancelotti side had been undone by precocious teenager Ayyoub Bouaddi.

    Sources indicate that ancelotti’s remarks about losing the midfield battle are from after a Champions League match in October 2024, when Lille shocked Real Madrid to end their 36-game unbeaten run. Bouaddi was at the heart of both statement results for his club and country.

    According to recent reports, COYP. 🦅 pic.twitter.com/78ZUj8SBOf.

    The second weekend of the Premier League season kicks off under the lights in South London as Crystal Palace host Manchester City at Selhurst Park. Manchester City won both fixtures 3-0 last season and they are in fact unbeaten in their last 11 Premier league away games against Crystal Palace, who have won just two of the 22 top flight meetings.

    According to recent reports, crystal Palace experienced defeat on the opening weekend, falling to a 2-0 loss at Everton last Saturday, meaning the Pierre Sage era started with a defeat. Tonight is Sage’s first home game in charge of the club.

    It has been revealed that “I think it will be a wonderful moment, but I prefer to have a wonderful moment with good news at the end of the game,” Sage said. “That is why I do not think about me in this situation. The most vital thing is the team and the result for sure, because we prepare all the week for that, to make them [the fans] happy. They will be happy to see us, but I think they would prefer to see us win. I will give my life to make them happy. I cannot do more. When you are in this stadium [Selhurst Park], you feel the history. You feel that there is something heavy weighing on you. It is a great responsibility that I have been entrusted with. We cannot wait to see this stadium in action.”.

    Sage has confirmed that Ismaila Sarr, who has been linked with a move away from the club this summer, and Chadi Riad will miss out tonight due to injury, as will striker Jean-Philippe Mateta. Palace have confirmed the addition of Axel Disasi on loan from Chelsea and the French defender could be involved tonight.

    Manchester City appeared to be heading towards defeat in Enzo Maresca’s first league game in charge of the club last weekend. They were 1-0 down at home against Bournemouth in the closing stages before goals from Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol gave them a come-from-behind win.

    It has been a busy week in the transfer window for Manchester City. Both Savio (formerly Savinho) and Omar Marmoush have left for Tottenham, joining a long list of departures from the Etihad this summer. Moroccan midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi has arrived in an £85m deal from Lille and has become the most expensive teenager in Premier League history. Maresca has confirmed that 18-year-old Bouaddi is ready to start.

    Industry observers note that “He [Bouaddi] is ready,” Maresca noted. “He was working with his former club so he is fit. We will see how long he needs in terms of adaptation but he is ready to go. He is quite calm. He does not look 18, he already looks older, which is important. But in this case, we need to go slowly because he is very young, he has come from a different country so there is no rush for him. He is going to help us now and in the future. He is very mature for being 18.”.

    Team news from Selhurst Park to follow shortly.
